intent_record.intent_summary: Extract power average calculation into a reusable helper function with zero-division guard to reduce code duplication and improve maintainability.
intent_record.what: Added a new static helper function `occ_get_powr_avg()` that takes a 64-bit accumulator and 32-bit sample count, returning zero if samples is zero, otherwise returning the result of `mul_u64_u32_div(accum, 1000000UL, samples)`.
intent_record.how: This function encapsulates power average calculation logic with built-in division-by-zero protection. It enables safe computation of average power by multiplying the accumulator by 1000000 and dividing by the sample count, preventing undefined behavior when samples equals zero.

intent_record.intent_summary: Extract inline power average calculation into a dedicated helper function occ_get_powr_avg() to improve code reusability and maintainability.
intent_record.what: Replaced inline division and multiplication calculation (val = get_unaligned_be32(&power->accumulator) / get_unaligned_be32(&power->update_tag); val *= 1000000ULL;) with a function call to occ_get_powr_avg() that takes the same two unaligned_be32 values as arguments.
intent_record.how: This change extracts the power average calculation logic into a dedicated helper function. The runtime behavior should remain identical if occ_get_powr_avg() implements the same division and multiplication logic internally, but it centralizes the calculation logic, making it reusable and easier to maintain or modify in one place.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unused helper function `occ_get_powr_avg()` to eliminate dead code and simplify the module.
intent_record.what: Removed the static function `occ_get_powr_avg()` which took two parameters (u64 accum, u32 samples) and returned a calculated power average value using conditional logic and multiplication/division.
intent_record.how: This function is no longer available for internal use within this compilation unit. Any code that previously called `occ_get_powr_avg()` must now either be refactored to use alternative logic or the function must be inlined/replaced at call sites. This reduces code size and eliminates an unused or redundant helper function.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the vulnerability root cause by extracting the power average calculation into a dedicated helper function with explicit zero-division protection (zero-division guard). This prevents the divide-by-zero crash in `occ_show_power_1()` when `update_tag` is zero, which occurs when no samples have been collected yet.

The group removes an unused helper function `occ_get_powr_avg()` for code cleanup. This is unrelated to the divide-by-zero vulnerability in `occ_show_power_1()`, which requires adding a zero-check on the `update_tag` variable before division. Removing dead code does not address the root cause of the crash.

candidates.rationale: This statement performs division by get_unaligned_be32(&power->update_tag) without checking if it is zero. When update_tag is zero (no samples collected yet), this causes a kernel divide-by-zero crash. The root cause is the missing zero-division check before the division operation.

The division operation at lines 444-445 lacks protection against zero divisor. When power->update_tag contains zero (early boot or no samples), the division triggers a kernel panic. This is the vulnerable code path that needs zero-division protection.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement performs division by get_unaligned_be32(&power->update_tag) without checking if the divisor is zero. When update_tag is zero (which occurs during early boot or when no samples have been collected yet), this division operation causes a kernel divide-by-zero crash. The root cause is the missing zero-division check before performing the division.
